areas_completed: Authoritative snapshot publication and absence semantics
areas_remaining: Owner control over replanning and execution

Authoritative snapshot publication and a.question: When does a newly scanned collection replace the working snapshot?
Authoritative snapshot publication and a.answer: Keep the last complete snapshot authoritative while exposing new-scan progress and failures separately; publish only a completed replacement.
options_presented: Publish complete scans only
Publish explicitly partial scans
Keep the complete snapshot and expose partial progress separately

Authoritative snapshot publication and a.question: Which per-entity failures invalidate a complete scan?
Authoritative snapshot publication and a.answer: Identity or ownership failure invalidates the entire current scan attempt. Optional fact failures such as capacity remain explicit unknown values and do not exclude the entity.
options_presented: Any field failure invalidates the scan
Accept entities without identity or ownership
Require identity and ownership while allowing optional facts to remain unknown

Authoritative snapshot publication and a.question: What happens when replacement scans keep failing?
Authoritative snapshot publication and a.answer: Retain the last complete snapshot, but after an evidence-derived staleness threshold block new decisions that depend on that snapshot.
options_presented: Use stale data indefinitely
Retain data but block dependent decisions after a threshold
Delete the snapshot after a threshold

Authoritative snapshot publication and a.question: How should absence and deletion work across all observed collections?
Authoritative snapshot publication and a.answer: Use a general Rust reconciliation policy: one absence from a complete set snapshot becomes missing_once; two consecutive complete-snapshot absences remove the entity; an explicit authoritative deletion removes it immediately; absence in failed or incomplete scans has no meaning; an unavailable field becomes stale or unknown without deleting the entity. Stations are the first proof, not a station-specific implementation.
options_presented: Remove after one complete-snapshot absence
Confirm absence in two consecutive complete snapshots
Never remove automatically

Cooperative native discovery.question: How should independently changing world data become one decision input?
Cooperative native discovery.answer: Partition observation into independently completed section revisions with capture windows, coverage, quality, and freshness. Freeze exact accepted section revisions into one immutable decision snapshot; do not claim a globally simultaneous X4 snapshot.
options_presented: One globally atomic galaxy scan
Independent completed sections composed into a frozen decision snapshot
Event streams only

Cooperative native discovery.question: How should Phase 05.1 prove the framework beyond stations?
Cooperative native discovery.answer: Add a developer-only heavy faction-ship PoC: a complete ship identity/ownership/type/location index plus independently refreshed cargo, crew, and loadout detail sections. Use the Phase 05.2 harness and do not admit its data to Faction Minds before it passes normal-speed and SETA evidence gates.
options_presented: Station collection only
Developer-only heavy ship candidate with partitioned details
Immediate production ship telemetry

Cooperative native discovery.question: How is game-thread work bounded across all collectors?
Cooperative native discovery.answer: Use one global scheduler and shared real-time CPU/native-work budget. Game-time age determines urgency; real elapsed cost limits permitted work. Under the observed approximately 6.2x SETA factor, prioritize overdue core indexes without multiplying heavy native stages. If the scheduler cannot keep up, mark sections stale and block dependent decisions.
options_presented: Independent per-collector quotas
One global scheduler with a shared budget
Run whole collectors sequentially

Cooperative native discovery.question: How are sections prioritized and degraded under load?
Cooperative native discovery.answer: Classify every section independently by measured read cost, rate of change, and decision-specific importance/freshness. Reserve capacity for identity, ownership, location, and core indexes; defer cargo, crew, loadout, or other details according to active decision dependencies and freshness targets.
options_presented: Defer detail sections before core indexes
Increase work until all sections catch up
Stop the whole observation cycle

Cooperative native discovery.question: What happens when an indivisible native enumeration stage causes a visible hitch?
Cooperative native discovery.answer: Reject that collector from production until a safe source is found. A one-time enumeration followed by events is acceptable only after event coverage for additions and removals is proven. Exact release thresholds come from normal-speed and SETA measurements; visible or simulation-budget-breaking hitches fail the gate.
options_presented: Reject the collector until a safe source exists
Allow one load-time hitch and then rely on events
Allow periodic hitches for completeness

Cooperative native discovery.question: What load shape should replace periodic full scans?
Cooperative native discovery.answer: Advance small bounded collector steps from a frequent frame, tick, or pulse source and continuously pump ready messages instead of creating an N-second collection spike. Collection scheduling and transport pumping are separate state machines even when one callback invokes both. The exact X4 callback seam remains evidence-gated.
options_presented: Run a full scan every N seconds and then transmit it
Advance a bounded continuous stream on frequent pulses
Collect continuously but transmit only after a full global snapshot

Pipe messages and queue headroom.question: How should complete observation records be packed into pipe messages?
Pipe messages and queue headroom.answer: Batch multiple complete records into each message, but never split one record across messages. Treat 256 KiB only as an X4 Live MCP precedent, not as a Live Galaxy limit; derive Live Galaxy's own hard ceiling from measured Lua allocation/copy cost, write latency, Rust decode cost, failure amplification, and queue memory.
options_presented: One object per message
Multiple complete records per message without splitting a record
Arbitrary byte chunking across messages
